text:
alex: rolled the A/B to 30% earlier, but telemetry shows a KV miss ratio spike and 5xx rate creeping on the canary path. I want to undo the traffic override ASAP.
maria: saw that alert too. Where are the misses coming from - prefix cache or session KV?
asl: ops-bot posted alert: [ALERT] canary-path.kv.miss_rate > 8% (5m) -> paged oncall
sam: quick check of logs shows `kv.get(prefix_session_*)` latency rising, TTLs look normal. Could be prefill not warming for new routing.
kevin: if prefill didn't run we should avoid a full disable that causes mass cache invalidations. Plan: 1) flip routing override to route 0% to canary (fast revert) 2) keep canary instances alive so in-memory KV isn't lost 3) run prefill on a small subset to warm hot keys 4) monitor errors for 5-10m then fully scale down.
maria: agree. How do we flip routing quickly? Is there a one-line for the console or do we need API?
alex: console has a 'force revert' button but it's gated. I'll run the internal API: `POST /internal/rollouts/{id}/override` with payload `{"pct": 0, "reason":"automatic-undo-kv-spike"}` — that will update traffic policy immediately.
sam: are we sure that will not trigger session affinity re-assignment that evicts caches? We should set `preserve_sessions=true` if possible.
kevin: good catch. Use: `/internal/rollouts/{id}/override?preserve_sessions=true` so we only change routing decisions for new requests. Existing connections stay.
alex: running command now: ```bash
curl -X POST "https://platform.internal/api/internal/rollouts/canary-2026-02/override?preserve_sessions=true" -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ADMIN_TOKEN}" -d '{"pct":0, "note":"undo due to kv-miss spike"}'
```
ops-bot: deploybot: rollout override updated by alex — traffic to canary set to 0% (preserve_sessions=true) :white_check_mark:
maria: nice. We still need to avoid cache TTL churn. Are there any background sweeps or cron jobs that will evict prefills when traffic drops?
sam: there's an auto-scale-down hook that runs 2m after traffic to zero and calls `node.shutdown(force=false)` which keeps in-memory cache for 30s then serializes to disk. That could cause cold-starts. We should patch the hook for canaries to delay scale-down by 10m.
kevin: Can we just mark the canary pool as 'hold' using the API to prevent autoscaler from acting? `/pools/{pool}/hold?reason=rollback`
alex: doing that now. ```bash
curl -X POST "https://platform.internal/api/pools/canary-pool/hold" -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ADMIN_TOKEN}" -d '{"reason":"rollback-keep-cache-warm"}'
```
ops-bot: pool hold applied to canary-pool by alex
maria: while that holds, let's kick off a targeted prefill for the top keys we're seeing misses for. Sam, can you list top 20 prefixes?
sam: pulling from recent spans... top prefixes: `user_session_`, `ctx_prompt_`, `shared_prefix_qa_` — I'll run prefill job: `jobs/prefill --keys-file=top-prefixes.txt --parallel=10`
kevin: remember to tag the job with `rollback-2026-02` so it doesn't get picked up by normal ttl reconciliation.
sam: done. Job started. Logs: ```json
{"job":"prefill","status":"running","prefilled":0}
```
alex: telemetry shows kv.miss_rate dropping from 9.2% -> 3.1% after prefill started (1m). 5xx rate trending down.
maria: good. After we confirm stability for 5-10m, do we want to do a safe disable of the canary route entirely or keep it as a baseline?
kevin: prefer to keep as a baseline with 0% traffic for now and gated canary restarts — that keeps caches warm and lets us A/B quickly. Only if we need capacity we'll scale pool down.
sam: note for postmortem: add a guard in rollout UI that warns when KV miss rate delta > 3% within 5m of traffic change. Could block % increases > 10% if cache heat isn't sufficient.
maria: agree. Also add a quick signal in console: 'prefill status' and 'pool hold' buttons visible during rollouts.
alex: I'll open an RFC and a small ticket: - add preserve_sessions flag to console revert button - expose pool hold toggle - add KV prefill job link in rollout details
kevin: and add a telemetry dashboard tile showing `kv.miss_rate`, `canary_5xx_rate`, and `traffic_pct` aligned on the same time axis.
sam: will draft the dashboard and reuse the prefill job association.
ops-bot: incident closed automatically (root cause mitigated)
maria: thanks everyone. Follow-ups: alex RFC, sam dashboard + job tagging, kevin autoscaler tweak (delay), i'll handle console UX. :thumbsup:
